name: 30 — migration_check FAILS → zero-residue abort, v1 still served (PR-6d, node-log validated)
description:
Single-node lazy migration whose `#[app::migration_check]` REJECTS the produced v2 root, triggering a LOGICAL ABORT with ZERO RESIDUE — the headline PR-6d soundness test.
The v2 fixture (`scenario-migration-check-fail-v2`) runs a deliberately **lossy** migrate: it drops the lexicographically smallest key, so exactly one item is lost. The migrate emits a transient `MigrationWitness` carrying the v1 item count (captured before the drop). Its `#[app::migration_check]` compares that baseline against the **produced** v2 count (read through the staging buffer) — they differ, so it returns `false`. The runtime then returns `Err(MigrationCheckFailed)` BEFORE `write_migration_state` and BEFORE finalize.
Staging discipline: the migrate's child-entry writes were buffered in the staging `ContextStorage` and are DROPPED on the failed check — they never reached the live store. So v1 is intact (root AND every child entry) with zero residue; there is no byte snapshot/restore. On the lazy path the failed migration is swallowed and the access PROCEEDS on the current (v1) application, so the triggering call SUCCEEDS serving pre-migration data.
Node-log validation (the explicit requirement for scenario 30):
  - `assert_log_present "migration_check failed: logical abort"` — the
    pre-commit check rejected the produced v2 root (PR-6d task 6d.3).
  - `assert_log_present "proceeding with current application"` — the lazy
    access fell back to v1 rather than committing v2 (logged as a failed
    ladder hop for marker-ed contexts, or a failed single jump for legacy
    marker-less ones).
  - `assert_log_absent "migration_check passed"` — the commit path was never
    taken.
Plus a behavioural assertion: a post-abort read still returns v1 schema (`1.0.0`) with ALL THREE original items — proving the app still serves v1.
Because migration_v2 defaults ON (PR-6b task 6b.8), the pre-commit check runs natively — no merobox feature flag is needed.
